title: The Little Motor
style: Chamber pop with a theatrical lyrical mezzo-soprano lead; intimate, story-forward verses over felt piano, pizzicato strings, cello, and restrained brushed percussion. Build each chorus with swelling chamber strings and close harmonies, then pivot into a salsa montuno-style bridge: syncopated piano montuno, hand percussion, lively bass tumbao, and answering vocal phrases. Return to a hushed, emotionally resolved outro. Detailed, warm acoustic production with clear vocal presence and dynamic arrangement.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Cali kept the heat past closing time
I wore my borrowed courage like a dress
You were twenty, with a stranger’s grin
We left the bar and made a small mess
The bed was bright, the promise less
I laughed and thought, there’s time to mend
Some nights are only meant to end

[Verse 2]
Mama called before the evening fell
“May God be with you”—soft across the line
I never learned to pray, but heard her pride
And all the years she’d wished I’d toe the line
I’d run through hidden rooms and borrowed names
Tonight her tenderness outshone the blame

[Chorus]
So let me keep the taste of every hour
The bitter shot, the rain-warm pavement stone
The little motor tucked beneath my coat
The careful dose I thought I could control
If this is all the world will let me hold
I’ll hold it close, I’ll hold it close

[Verse 3]
The forms were stacked beside the waiting chair
A box to mark: wake me, or let me sleep
If engines failed, while breathing still went on
Would I want my final vigil deep?
For weeks I turned the question in my hands
Then chose the dark that asked no last demands

[Chorus]
So let me keep the taste of every hour
The bitter shot, the rain-warm pavement stone
The little motor tucked beneath my coat
The careful dose I thought I could control
If this is all the world will let me hold
I’ll hold it close, I’ll hold it close

[Bridge]
Piano calls, and the room answers back
One hand says go, one hand says stay
Cali, take this name and carry it
I spent my years in flight; tonight I choose the way
Ay, vida, bend and turn
Ay, vida, let the old days burn
Not the mother’s voice, not the green hillside
Just the life I wore before the door swung wide

[Final Chorus]
I tried to smell the world on the road out
Even the sharp things, even diesel, dust
I counted every blue between the roofs
Every green leaf taking morning on trust
Thirty-three years folded small inside my coat
I kept this day; the rest I let it go

[Outro]
If no one finds the ground we’re dreaming of
Let me go unwoken, wrapped in what I chose
And somewhere in the engines’ distant hush
My mother’s blessing travels where I go
